beats: In 1518, a city's cure for people who couldn't stop dancing was… more dancing!
It's July in Strasbourg, and a woman named Frau Troffea steps into the street and starts to dance.
She dances all day, all night, for days, and she can't stop.
Within a week, dozens of people have joined her.
This is the Dancing Plague of 1518.
The city's doctors decide it's a natural disease, caused by hot blood.
So the council opens the guild halls and builds a wooden stage for the dancers.
They even hire musicians, and strong men to hold the dancers up!
One chronicle says four hundred people were dancing within a month.
So the council does a U-turn and bans public dancing and music!
The dancers are loaded into wagons and sent to a mountain shrine of Saint Vitus, to pray.
By September, the dancing finally stops.
Today, most historians blame mass panic, after years of famine and disease.
But in 1518, the cure for dancing… was more dancing!
